goal: reproduce Caura published headline (caura-500-opaque-compact) on the 60 Q

published_flags.run: --skip-ingest --chunk-mode turns --agent-prefix lmeo --sibling-expansion --sibling-window 0 --context-budget 150000 --raw-turns-only --no-as-of-recall --context-format compact --pipeline agentic-v1 --reader gemini --reader-model gemini-3.8-flash --judge openai --judge-model gpt-4o --secondary-judge gemini --secondary-judge-model gemini-3.5-flash-lite --concurrency 5 --question-ids <ids>

embedder_serving: bge-m3 via HF TEI image text-embeddings-inference:hopper-1.8 on a SHARED H100 MIG slice next to Mem0's qwen-tei; compose project caura-tei-gpu, host port 127.0.0.1:8100, reached by core-api as http://tei-gpu:80/v1
enrichment_tokens_method: derived from measured rate (2943 in / 142 out per memory); server image is baked (no per-call token logging available without a rebuild)

server_tuning.note: raised from the 2/second default (core_api rate_limit_write_bulk) so 5 concurrent /memories/bulk writes pass at ingest concurrency 5; admission throttling only — no effect on stored memories or results

deviations_from_published: Embedder served on a GPU MIG slice SHARED with Mem0's running qwen-tei (published: dedicated GPU TEI). Same model/vectors.
Enrichment via the Gemini API key (gemini-3.1-flash-lite) not the published Vertex endpoint; same model.
harness_reliability_patches: caura.py recall (/search): retry budget raised to 8 attempts with a 30s backoff cap so a brief core-storage/DB restart is ridden out; a 5xx/429 that still survives now RAISES CauraRecallError instead of returning [] (the silent empty-context -> blind-answer bug that invalidated lme_caura_default_60q). Speed/reliability only — the 200 path is unchanged, so healthy-run results are identical.
run_lme.sh: assert_retrieval_nonempty() aborts the run before the paid judge if any answered question retrieved 0 candidates.

reuses_artifacts.note: answer-only rerun on the store that this run already ingested; artifacts below are REFERENCED, not copied. The live Caura store (agent_prefix lmeo-*) is the one ingested by that run; the pre-checks verified it still holds the 60 agents.

models_note: The 'models' block above recorded only entity extraction as 'enrichment' and MISSED the gpt-5.4-nano memory-creation LLM that did the bulk of ingest work. 'models_actual' is the complete, corrected list.

models_actual.role: memory creation (write-path classifier: auto-classifies type/weight/title/summary on every write)
models_actual.note: USE_LLM_FOR_MEMORY_CREATION=true; the write-path classifier defaults to provider=OpenAI (business_classifier.py: `provider or ProviderName.OPENAI`) and model=gpt-5.4-nano (common/llm/constants.py LLM_FALLBACK_MODEL_OPENAI). We pinned ONLY entity extraction to gemini and left PLATFORM_LLM_* unset, so this fell to OpenAI. DOMINANT ingest LLM: 40,654 calls vs 12,352 gemini. Authors used gemini-3.1-flash-lite via Vertex (REPRODUCE.md line 18).

models_actual.role: entity extraction / graph (async-derived; derived memories dropped in turn mode)

cost_actual_usd.sources: Dollar figures are from the provider BILLING pages (Google AI Studio per-model spend; OpenAI Usage per-model); per-run splits use the harness's EXACT recorded reader-token shares. Judge $ is estimated (harness does not record judge tokens). Gemini totals are all-Caura (Mem0 never used the Gemini key). gpt-5.4-nano and gemini spend span BOTH Caura runs; attributed below.

answering_answer2.basis: reader = 62% of the $3.43 gemini-3.8-flash billing total (answer2 = 1.725M of 2.81M input tok); judge est.

cost_actual_usd.background_reprocessing: Nov 26 00:00-05:53 UTC gpt-5.4-nano (~$6.70) was BACKGROUND re-processing of memory-creation/enrichment tasks the Nov-25 DB crashes left pending (core-operations 'entity extraction re-run / lost'). Caused by the DB crashes, NOT the experiment design. It is ingest work, not answering, and ran almost entirely OUTSIDE the answer2 window (0 gpt-5.4-nano calls inside 04:17-04:23).

NOT_this_run.text-embedding-3-small_$0.0076: Mem0 / old variant-2, not this run (we used local bge-m3)
NOT_this_run.gpt-5.4-nano_is_ours: yes — it IS this run's memory-creation LLM on the Caura OpenAI key

cost_actual_usd.note: This run reused the store ingested by lme_caura_default_60q_INVALID_retrieval0 (--skip-ingest), so its OWN spend is only the 'answering_answer2' block (~$2.2). 'ingest_one_time' is shown for the full-pipeline cost.
